sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: NFAT-luciferase reporter assay in DT40 cells: tagged GPVI signaling activity comparable to wild-type GPVI; expression level comparable to wild-type by supplemental blot (L7); single-molecule surface imaging confirmed surface display (L4).
sites.rationale: GPVI is a type I transmembrane protein with a 20-residue signal peptide (residues 1–20) and a single extracellular face spanning residues 21–269; the only unambiguous extracellular terminus is the mature N-terminus beginning at Q21. The ledger clips (L3–L8) report SNAP-tag and HaloTag insertions 'in the extracellular region' of full-length GPVI but name no specific residue or loop, so the position is topology-derived: insert_after_residue = 20 (last signal-peptide residue A20), placing the tag immediately before Q21, 249 residues from the TM boundary. Residues confirmed by reading the numbered sequence: residue 20 = A, residue 21 = Q. Full-length GPVI bearing extracellular SNAP-tag and HaloTag fusions was transiently expressed in CHO-K1 cells and DT40 chicken B cells; single-molecule surface imaging confirmed receptor display and an NFAT-luciferase reporter assay confirmed signaling activity comparable to wild-type GPVI.

sources.claim: The functionality of the tagged receptors was shown ( Figure 1 D) using an NFAT reporter assay. 33 Figure 1.

literature_notes: L3–L8 all describe the same experimental system (SNAP-tag/HaloTag on extracellular GPVI) from a preprint (L3, L7, L8) and its published counterpart (L4, L5, L6); no specific residue or named loop is given in any clip, so the junction is topology-derived at the sole extracellular terminus (after signal-peptide cleavage). L1 and L2 describe a C-terminal Myc tag on full-length GPVI; the C-terminus (residue 339) is intracellular (topology landmarks: IC 290–339) and is therefore recorded in other_positions only.

literature_other_positions.note: Myc epitope tag placed at the C-terminus of full-length GPVI in pcDNA3.1; residue 339 falls within the intracellular domain (290–339) and is not accessible on the extracellular face.
